title: Lakers @ Spurs — Norm Nixon free-throw fake mishandled; protest upheld, last 3 seconds replayed, Spurs win 117-114 (Nov 30, 1982 - Apr 1983)
incident_summary: With San Antonio leading 116-114 and seconds left in regulation, Lakers guard Norm Nixon faked his second free-throw attempt, drawing players from both teams into the lane. The officials called a double lane violation and ordered a jump ball (at halfcourt/center court) instead of requiring Nixon to re-shoot the free throw. The Lakers won the tap and Nixon scored the tying basket at the buzzer to force overtime; Los Angeles eventually won 137-132 in double overtime. San Antonio protested that the officials misapplied the rules; in December 1982 Commissioner Larry O'Brien upheld the protest. The final three seconds of regulation were replayed before the teams' next scheduled meeting in April 1983, and the Spurs won the replayed finish 117-114.
scoring_play: Nixon second free-throw attempt (faked; never properly re-shot) followed by a jump ball and Nixon's tying field goal at the buzzer — the tying basket was later voided by the upheld protest and replay.

cause.detail: Confirmed misapplication of the playing rules by the officiating crew: faking a free throw should have resulted in Nixon re-shooting rather than a jump ball. (USA Today protest-history recap; LA Times.)
